intended_object: The constant c(x) = (b−a)⁻¹ ∫ₐᵇ [(k⋆w)(x,s) − ∫ₐˢ (k⋆r)(x,q) dq] ds. It is chosen so that c(x) + ∫ₐᵗ (k⋆r)(x,q) dq equals the mollified field k⋆w almost everywhere in time. The docstring and the uses in the file (lpsPrim, lps_prim_ae_eq) make this its role.
explanation:
This definition is not a standard mathematical notion. It is a helper constant inside one proof. The proof shows that a function of time with a weak derivative is absolutely continuous: it equals a constant plus the integral of its derivative.

The constant comes from averaging over (a, b) the difference between the function and its primitive started at a. That difference is almost everywhere constant, so its average gives the right value. The constant exists only to define `lpsPrim` and prove `lps_prim_ae_eq` for the Escauriaza–Seregin–Šverák argument.

It has no counterpart in the literature or in Mathlib beyond being this particular expression. The body does compute the constant the docstring describes: the time-average over Ioo a b of `vlConvT k w x s - ∫ q in a..s, vlConvT k r x q`.
